h2. Objective

Time-boxed research spike to investigate and evaluate the migration approach for Unite Enrollment automation assets identified in QA-995.

* Evaluate compatibility of existing feature files with the target automation framework
* Assess step definition reusability and refactoring needs
* Investigate config/property file migration strategy
* Review SQL scripts and test data portability
* Identify tooling or framework gaps that need to be addressed
* Estimate effort for full migration based on inventory from QA-995

h2. Expected Outcomes

* Technical recommendation document for migration approach
* Effort estimation (T-shirt sizing) per module/service
* Identified risks and mitigation strategies
* Dependency map (tools, environments, access requirements)
* Go/No-Go recommendation for migration execution

* Migration approach documented with pros/cons of at least 2 alternatives
* Effort estimate provided for each identified asset category
* Blockers and dependencies clearly listed
* Recommendation reviewed by team lead
* Linked to QA-995 as reference

h2. 📋 EnrollmentKT.pdf — Knowledge Transfer Summary

h3. What is MSC Enrollment?

The *MSC Enrollment* is a mobile app step-by-step REST microservice ({{unite-enrollment}}) that guides a prospect through an event-driven flow:

{quote}*Prospect → Owner → Beneficiary → Bank → Allocations → Review → Account Created*{quote}

It's one of three enrollment systems in the Ascensus 529 landscape (MSC API, Universal Platform Web, Legacy JSP — this doc covers MSC only).

----

h3. 🏗️ Architecture

The enrollment BFF (cloud host) sits between the mobile app/Postman/Rest Assured and five downstream services:

* *Account API* — verify prospects, create account
* *Auth API* — issue {{ENROLL_PROSPECT}} JWT
* *Metadata API* — plans, states, funds
* *Profile API* — owner/beneficiary verification
* *Bank API* — routing number validation

----

h3. 🔄 Enrollment Flow (13 Steps)

||Step||Action||Auth||
|01|GET Certificate (RSA for encryption)|None|
|05|POST Create Prospect → issues JWT|None|
|06–12|Owner, Address, Beneficiary, Bank, Allocations|{{ENROLL_PROSPECT}} JWT|
|13|Review-Confirm → Account Created|{{ENROLL_PROSPECT}} JWT|

*Critical:* State must be chained via {{correlationId}}, {{eventId}}, {{seqNum}} between every step.

----

h3. 🔐 JWT Roles

* {{ENROLL_PROSPECT}} — issued after Step 05, required for Steps 06–13
* {{MEMBER}} — *blocked* on enrollment topic (returns 401)
* {{ACCEPTANCE_TEST}} — for Cucumber/local tests only

----

h3. 🌍 Environments

||Env||Enrollment BFF||
|QC4|{{unite-bff-cloud.qc4.unite529.com}}|
|Stage1|{{unite-bff-cloud.stage1.unite529.com}}|

Common plans: {{okdirect}}, {{njdirect}}, {{nmdirect}}, {{hawaii}}, {{unique}}

----

h3. 🤖 Automation Coverage

||Flow||Postman||Rest Assured||Cucumber||
|GET Plans|✅|❌ (recommended first target)|✅|
|Create Prospect|✅|❌|✅|
|Owner/Bank/Allocations|✅|❌|✅|
|Review-Confirm|✅|❌|✅|
|Universal Platform {{/accounts/}}|✅|✅ (12+ classes)|N/A|

*Recommended automation roadmap:*

# {{GET /plans/{planId}}} — read-only, lowest risk
# {{POST /enrollments/prospects}} — needs encryption + backend health
# Full E2E event chain — mirror {{run-flow.ps1}} in Rest Assured

----

h2. 🔧 TROUBLESHOOTING.pdf — Current Failure Analysis

h3. ⚠️ Active Issue: Create Prospect returning 500 (2/9 steps PASS)

The root cause is {{AccountGateway.verifyProspects}} failing — the enrollment BFF cannot reach {{POST /accountapi/v1/members/verify/prospects}}. This is a *backend/platform issue*, not a Postman collection issue.

*Verified failures (2026-07-29):*

||Env||Plan||requestId||
|QC4|okdirect|{{70ed971f-74c3-49b3-b499-80091eced363}}|
|QC4|hawaii|{{e6d27786-ffad-4d54-940f-f058729663e0}}|
|Stage1|okdirect|{{98a5b1e3-d436-4036-baf2-e3633411eb18}}|
|Stage1|hawaii|{{f8774e6f-9a97-4daa-85ed-50e0bab76fcf}}|

Both plans failing on both environments confirms this is *not plan-specific* — it's a backend connectivity issue.

----

h3. 🛠️ Workaround: {{jwtTokenManual}}

When Step 04 (Create Prospect) returns 500, you can bypass it by capturing an {{ENROLL_PROSPECT}} JWT from the mobile app:

# Start enrollment in the MSC mobile app (or via browser DevTools on {{okd.stage1.acs529.com}})
# Capture {{x-enc-jwttoken}} from the response header using Charles/Fiddler/DevTools
# Paste into Postman env variable {{jwtTokenManual}}
# Run: {{.\run-flow.ps1 -EnvName stage1 -PlanId okdirect -JwtTokenManual "eyJhbGci..."}}

*⚠️ Important:* Verify the JWT role is {{ENROLL_PROSPECT}} (not {{MEMBER}}) using the DEBUG - Decode jwtToken step in Postman.

----

column1: [V3][Universal Enrollment] Stabilize Flaky Automation Test Case for Member Withdrawal
column35:
The automated test case for *Member Withdrawal* in the Universal Enrollment (V3) application is exhibiting intermittent failures, resulting in inconsistent regression execution results. The objective of this story is to investigate the root cause of the flaky behavior, implement necessary fixes, and ensure the test executes reliably across environments and regression runs.

This effort will improve automation stability, reduce false failures, and increase confidence in regression test results.

----

h3. *Business Value*

* Improve regression suite reliability.
* Reduce false-positive automation failures.
* Improve CI/CD pipeline stability.
* Minimize manual investigation efforts during regression cycles.
* Increase confidence in Member Withdrawal functionality validation.

----

h3. *Scope*

* Analyze failure patterns from recent executions.
* Identify root causes (timing issues, test data dependency, environment dependency, synchronization issues, API/UI instability, etc.).
* Implement required automation fixes.
* Enhance logging and reporting where necessary.
* Validate test stability through multiple consecutive executions.
* Update automation documentation as needed.

----

h3. *Acceptance Criteria*

# Root cause of flaky behavior is identified and documented.
# Required automation fixes are implemented.
# Test passes consistently in at least *5 consecutive executions* without failure.
# No hardcoded wait or unstable locator remains in the test.
# Test execution results are documented and shared with the team.
# Regression suite completes successfully with the updated test.

*Description*

*This story focuses on validating the Mobile2 Ugift functionality, which allows members to create and retrieve Ugift IDs for eligible accounts.*

*The feature ensures:*

* *Ugift ID is generated only for eligible account types (Regular accounts)*
* *Restricted account types (Matching Grant, Kids accounts) do not allow Ugift creation*
* *Existing Ugift IDs are reused instead of creating duplicates*
* *Ugift information is correctly returned while accessing the Ugift page*

* *PATCH /mobile2/accounts/{ext}/ugift*
* *GET /mobile2/accounts/ugift*

* *Given account type = R*

* *Then:*
** *Ugift ID should be generated*

** *Ugift ID should NOT be created*

* *Then:*
** *Ugift ID should NOT be created*

** *Correct ugiftId*

*✅ AC6: Closed Account Handling*

* *If account is closed*

** *isClosedAcct = true*

----

*✅ AC7: Multiple Accounts Support*

Symptom: Universal Enrollment and partial enrollment failed on Stage1 (V2 multi-module regression + V3 UE suite). UI showed connectivity issues / functionality not available; API returned HTTP 500 System error; automation reported Database results are empty.

Root cause: Inserts into UII0.TU_PERSON and UII0.TU_BENE failed because CTL_INS_DTTM was NULL. These columns are populated by database triggers (TRG_TU_PERSON_BIUR, TRG_TU_BENE_BIUR). Both triggers were disabled in the UII0 schema, so insert-time audit timestamps were not set → ORA-01400: cannot insert NULL into ("UII0"."TU_PERSON"."CTL_INS_DTTM") / ("UII0"."TU_BENE"."CTL_INS_DTTM") (ORA-06512).

Fix: Triggers re-enabled on affected tables in UII0 (Swapnil Patil). Enrollment/account-open path expected to succeed once triggers are active.

h2. Context

Epic *SYN-443* delivers a barcode enhancement to automate the *Mailstop* process for returned mail across *529 and ABLE* plans. ODS/Kofax scans a barcode; the scan hits a *Unite GET API* that returns customer/mail details.

Performance testing was not completed before release planning. QA Automation is delivering a *lightweight QC4 baseline* (one endpoint) by *2026-07-31*, using the existing JMeter/Blaze perf toolchain. Synergy dev team (Suresh Mahto) owns the API; Rajib Akhter must confirm *QC4 vs Stage* test strategy before results are treated as release evidence.

*KB / artifacts:* {{qa-automation-kb/BarcodeProject/}}

h2. User outcome

As a *performance engineer*, I want a *validated Postman request and JMeter baseline* for the barcode lookup GET API in QC4, so that Synergy can prove the endpoint meets agreed load/latency targets before production release.

h2. Scope

*In:*

* Convert dev-provided *curl* → Postman collection (QC4 environment)
* Configure *client certificate* for QC4 Postman calls (wildcard {{*.localdev.acs529.com}} — credentials via private channel, not in repo)
* Validate *HTTP 200* and response schema with sample {{barcode_id}} from QC4 {{tu_sent_mail}}
* Author *JMeter* (or Blaze/Taurus) script for single GET endpoint
* Run baseline load test in QC4 per agreed profile (see KB {{docs/03-load-profile.md}})
* Document setup, results, limitations (QC4 auth bypass vs Stage/Prod cert path)
* Daily status to Brenda; environment decision recorded after Rajib approval

*Out:*

* Stage/Prod perf runs (blocked: cert + DevOps passcode policy unless Rajib approves alternate path)
* UI / Kofax scanner testing
* Functional regression of Mailstop business workflow beyond API response

QC4 · Unite MSC / IDP Login (Prime V3 IDP Login suite and manual login).

* Login page loads with branding and login panel shell.

* Users cannot authenticate; automation cannot enter credentials.

Username and password input fields display in the login form; user can enter credentials and proceed with authentication.

*Actual behavior*
Input fields are missing; login flow is blocked at the first step.

Here’s a clear description and acceptance criteria you can paste into QA-1052.

----

*Description*

This spike is to investigate the existing JMeter performance test scripts for the UNITE-MSC Login Flow and determine the effort required to create/extend performance test cases for this flow.

Scope of this spike includes:

* Identifying any existing JMeter scripts related to UNITE-MSC login (or similar login flows) and reviewing their current coverage and reusability.
* Understanding the end-to-end UNITE-MSC Login Flow (all key steps, parameters, correlations, and dependencies).
* Assessing what changes or new scripts are needed to support performance test coverage for:
** Successful login
** Common negative/edge scenarios (invalid credentials, lockout, etc. – only at a high level, not full implementation).
* Identifying any technical gaps, test data requirements, environment prerequisites, and external dependencies.
* Providing a rough ETA and approach to:
** Update/reuse existing scripts where possible.
** Create new JMeter test cases where necessary.
* Documenting findings and recommended next steps for actual implementation stories.

Deliverable for this spike: a short write‑up (Confluence page or attachment/comment on this ticket) summarizing findings, feasibility, risks, and ETA for creating the performance test cases.

----

*Acceptance Criteria*

# *Existing Assets Identified*
#* A list of all existing JMeter scripts relevant to login/authentication is documented (script names, locations/repos, and ownership).
#* For each relevant script, its current status (usable as-is, needs modification, or not reusable) is clearly stated.
# *Login Flow Understanding Documented*
#* The end-to-end UNITE-MSC Login Flow is documented at a high level, including:
#** Entry URL(s) and main HTTP requests.
#** Required headers/parameters and any dynamic values/correlations.
#** Dependencies on external services (e.g., SSO, authentication APIs).
#* Any environment or configuration dependencies (e.g., test URLs, certificates, feature flags) are identified.
# *Gap & Feasibility Analysis Completed*
#* Gaps between existing scripts and the desired UNITE-MSC Login Flow coverage are explicitly listed.
#* It is clearly stated whether current scripts can be:
#** Reused with minimal changes,
#** Require major rework, or
#** Need to be rebuilt from scratch.
# *ETA & Effort Estimate Provided*
#* A high-level ETA (in working days or story points) is provided for:

column35:
Users should be able to change their account password from their profile’s security settings after they are already authenticated into the system. This flow is part of standard account maintenance and does not require any MFA challenge because the user is already logged in and verified.

The system must require the *current password*, enforce password policy rules, and securely update the password.
column76:
h3. *1. Access Path*

* User navigates to: *Profile → Security → Change Password*.
* “Change Password” option is visible only to authenticated users.

h3. *2. Form Requirements*

The Change Password form must contain:

* Current password
* New password
* Confirm new password

h3. *3. Validation*

* System verifies the current password is correct.
* New password must meet full password policy.
* New password must match the confirmation field.
* User cannot reuse the same current password (if policy disallows).

h3. *4. Password Update*

* Upon validation, system updates password successfully.
* User receives a success message and a confirmation notification (optional based on system settings).

* Objective:  
Investigate existing Legacy Login Flow JMeter scripts and estimate the effort and timeline (ETA) to create the required test cases (TCs).
* Scope:
** Identify and review all current JMeter scripts related to the Legacy Login Flow.
** Assess script coverage against current business and technical requirements.
** Evaluate script maintainability, reusability, and alignment with existing performance testing standards.
** Define the list of new/updated JMeter test cases needed for the Legacy Login Flow.
** Provide a clear ETA and effort estimate for creating or updating these test cases.
* Activities:
** Collect and catalog existing Legacy Login Flow JMeter scripts from the repository/tooling used by the team.
** Analyze current parameterization, correlation, assertions, and data dependencies in the scripts.
** Map existing scripts to functional flows (e.g., valid login, invalid login, lockout, password reset entry points, etc.).
** Identify gaps in coverage, broken/obsolete flows, and any environment or data constraints.
** Validate compatibility of current scripts with the latest application version and test environments.
** Estimate effort to:
*** Fix or refactor existing scripts (if needed).
*** Create new JMeter scripts/TCS for uncovered scenarios.
*** Set up test data and configurations.
** Document findings, risks, assumptions, and final ETA.
* Deliverables:
** Inventory of existing Legacy Login Flow JMeter scripts and their current status (working/needs-fix/obsolete).
** Gap analysis of current vs. required test coverage for the Legacy Login Flow.
** Proposed list of JMeter test cases (TCs) to be created or updated.
** ETA and effort breakdown (e.g., person-days per task) for creating/updating TCs.
** Short recommendation note on next steps (e.g., prioritization, ownership, and any dependencies).

column1: [UNITE-MSC][Mobile2][CICD] QC4 API validation pipeline — Mobile Dashboard vertical slice (expand to all features)
column35:
h2. Goal

Stand up *QC4 CI pipeline* for *Mobile2 REST API validation* in the {{jsonapi-mobile-mobile2}} framework (TestNG + RestAssured), starting with *Mobile Dashboard* as the reference vertical slice, then expanding to all remaining mobile2 Cucumber feature areas.

This sprint: fix *dashboard* end-to-end in QC4 (connectivity → auth → API test green). Follow-on: replicate pipeline pattern for other features.

h2. Background

* Cucumber coverage exists in {{unite-mobile2}} (UniteMSC); new framework validates API responses via TestNG ({{MobileDashboardRequestTest}}, etc.).
* *Knowledge base* documents API → DB mapping, endpoints, auth flow: {{qa-automation-kb/mobile2-api-db-validation/}}
* *QC4 mobile login* was restored (RT 514351). Verified auth + dashboard via curl against {{unite-bff-wtn.qc4.unite529.com}}.
* Initial pipeline failure was {{java.net.ConnectException: Connection refused}} at {{getMobileToken}} — runner could not reach BFF (wrong host in properties vs. pod network), not missing GitHub secrets.

h2. Scope — Phase 1 (this sprint)

*Feature:* Mobile Dashboard ({{mobiledashboard.feature}} reference)

||Step||Endpoint||Method||
|Auth / JWT|{{/mobile1api/v1/mobilemembersession}}|POST|
|Dashboard|{{/mobile2api/v1/mobiledashboard}}|GET|
|YTD (later in same feature)|{{/mobile2api/v1/mobileytdsummary/{ext}}}|GET|

*QC4 BFF base URL (authoritative for pipeline):*

{{https://unite-bff-wtn.qc4.unite529.com}}

*Test class (framework):*

{{mobile2.dashboard.MobileDashboardRequestTest#getMobileDashboard}}

*Test plan:* {{okdirect}} (loaded via {{DatabaseResourceManager}})

h2. Scope — Phase 2 (subsequent stories / same epic)

Expand QC4 pipeline to remaining mobile2 features (priority order from KB {{STATUS.md}}):

# mobilebank, mobilecontribution, mobileactivity
# mobileTransactionHistory, mobilePerformance, mobileBalanceTrend
# investment, mobileStackup, mobileugift, planselection
# contentservice (external CMS — no DB validation)
# e2e (cross-feature index)

Full endpoint registry: {{mobile2-api-db-validation/mappings/endpoint-registry.yaml}}

h2. Auth model (NON_IDP — okdirect)

*No GitHub secret / Bearer token required upfront* for member session POST.

Required headers:

* {{Content-Type: application/json}}
* {{X-App-Version: 3.9.0}} (or framework app version)

Body: {{planId}}, {{username}}, {{password}} → response JWT at {{_embedded.item.jwtToken}}

Dashboard GET uses: {{Authorization: Bearer {jwtToken}}} + {{X-App-Version}}

*No HTTP proxy* expected for {{*.unite529.com}} from on-prem GitHub runner pod (direct route).

h2. Pipeline / DevOps requirements

h3. Environment config

||Property / setting||Value / notes||
|BFF host|{{https://unite-bff-wtn.qc4.unite529.com}}|
|Mobile1 API prefix|{{/mobile1api/v1/}}|
|Mobile2 API prefix|{{/mobile2api/v1/}}|
|Environment profile|QC4 ({{qc4.properties}} or equivalent)|
|{{-Dapi.host}}|Must match BFF host; confirm {{qc4.properties}} does not override to {{localhost:8443}} at runtime|
|Token URL property|Confirm {{MobileServerClient.getMobileToken}} uses same BFF host (may differ from {{api.host}})|
|Proxy|Not required for [unite529.com|http://unite529.com]; RestAssured ignores {{HTTP_PROXY}} env unless Java {{-Dhttps.proxyHost}} set|
|Secrets|Test creds in test data / properties for okdirect; no OAuth client secret for NON_IDP auth probe|

h3. Pre-flight probe (run inside pod before Maven)

*Step 1 — Auth (expect HTTP 200, jwtToken in body):*

{noformat}curl -sk -X POST "https://unite-bff-wtn.qc4.unite529.com/mobile1api/v1/mobilemembersession" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-App-Version: 3.9.0" \
  -d '{"planId":"okdirect","username":"QAMSCAUTO_REG_1234567890","password":"Newton@123"}'{noformat}

*Step 2 — Extract JWT (if jq available):*

{noformat}JWT=$(curl -sk -X POST "https://unite-bff-wtn.qc4.unite529.com/mobile1api/v1/mobilemembersession" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "X-App-Version: 3.9.0" \
  -d '{"planId":"okdirect","username":"QAMSCAUTO_REG_1234567890","password":"Newton@123"}' \
  | jq -r '._embedded.item.jwtToken')
echo "JWT length: ${#JWT}"{noformat}

*Step 3 — Dashboard (expect HTTP 200):*

{noformat}curl -sk -w "\nHTTP_CODE:%{http_code}\n" \
  -X GET "https://unite-bff-wtn.qc4.unite529.com/mobile2api/v1/mobiledashboard" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer ${JWT}" \
  -H "X-App-Version: 3.9.0"{noformat}

*Probe interpretation:*

* *200* → BFF reachable from pod; proceed to Maven
* *Connection refused* → pod → BFF network/routing (DevOps), not test assertion failure
* *ECONNRESET* → infra/LB issue (see RT 514351 pattern)

h3. Local / CI Maven commands (framework repo)

Run from {{jsonapi-mobile-mobile2}} module root:

{noformat}# Single dashboard test (QC4 profile — adjust -P/-D to match repo conventions)
mvn test -Dtest=MobileDashboardRequestTest#getMobileDashboard -Dspring.profiles.active=qc4{noformat}

If properties file driven:

{noformat}mvn test -Dtest=MobileDashboardRequestTest#getMobileDashboard \
  -Dapi.host=https://unite-bff-wtn.qc4.unite529.com{noformat}

Confirm actual profile names with Chaitanya ({{qc4.properties}}, Maven {{-P}} flags in {{ags-unitemsc}} workflow).

h3. GitHub Actions / workflow checklist

* Run auth curl probe as first job step (fail fast on network)
* Set BFF base URL in workflow env or properties (not localhost)
* Log resolved token URL / api.host at test startup (diagnostics)
* On-prem runner pod can reach {{unite-bff-wtn.qc4.unite529.com:443}} (no proxy)
* Publish Surefire report artifact on failure
* Document okdirect test member availability in QC4

h2. API validation flow (dashboard)

{noformat}POST /mobile1api/v1/mobilemembersession  →  JWT (_embedded.item.jwtToken)
GET  /mobile2api/v1/mobiledashboard      →  MobileDashboard (HAL _embedded.item){noformat}

Downstream (for future API–DB compare, not blocking Phase 1 pipeline):

* Account, Profile, Metadata gateways → see KB {{docs/02-features/mobiledashboard/overview.md}}
* SQL validation queries: {{sql/account/}}, {{sql/profile/}}, {{sql/metadata/}}, {{sql/composite/mobiledashboard/}}

h2. Known failure modes

||Symptom||Likely cause||Owner||
|Connection refused at getMobileToken|Wrong host (localhost:8443) or pod cannot reach BFF|DevOps / Chaitanya — properties + network|
|ECONNRESET|LB / BFF down|Platform (RT)|
|401/403 with HTTP response|Auth/creds/JWT claims|QA + framework config|
|Assertion on dashboard fields|Test data / API response mismatch|QA — compare with KB {{@md1}} scenario|

h2. References

||Resource||Path / link||
|KB README|{{qa-automation-kb/mobile2-api-db-validation/README.md}}|
|Dashboard overview|{{docs/02-features/mobiledashboard/overview.md}}|
|Endpoint registry|{{mappings/endpoint-registry.yaml}}|
|Auth flow|{{docs/01-shared/auth-and-session.md}}|
|Architecture|{{docs/00-architecture/bff-orchestration-flow.md}}|
|QC4 login incident|{{ISSUES/06242026/}} (RT 514351)|
|UniteMSC feature (read-only)|{{mobiledashboard.feature}}, {{MobileDashboardStepdefs.java}}|

h2. Out of scope (this story)

* Modifying UniteMSC source repos
* Full API–DB SQL compare in CI (Phase 1 = API smoke green; DB validation KB continues in parallel)

column35:
h2. Environment

* QC4

h2. Problem

Mobile member login is not working in QC4. Both the mobile app and Postman fail at authentication.

*Endpoint:* POST /mobile1api/v1/mobilemembersession

*URL:* [https://mobileapi.qc4.acs529.com/mobile1api/v1/mobilemembersession|https://mobileapi.qc4.acs529.com/mobile1api/v1/mobilemembersession]

*Alternate app BFF host:* [https://unite-bff-wtn.qc4.unite529.com/mobile1api/v1/|https://unite-bff-wtn.qc4.unite529.com/mobile1api/v1/]

*Error (Postman):* {{Error: write ECONNRESET}}

Connection reset before any HTTP status is returned.

h2. Steps to reproduce

# Open Postman (Desktop Agent).
# POST to [https://mobileapi.qc4.acs529.com/mobile1api/v1/mobilemembersession|https://mobileapi.qc4.acs529.com/mobile1api/v1/mobilemembersession]
# Headers: Content-Type: application/json, Authorization: Bearer [acceptance JWT] (if required by collection)
# Body (JSON):

{noformat}{
  "planId": "upromise",
  "username": "<QC4 test member>",
  "password": "<password>"
}{noformat}

# Send request.

_(Optional: select only the JSON lines above → toolbar </> → language JSON.)_

h2. Expected

* HTTP 200 with MobileMemberSession (session id + JWT), OR documented 401/403 JSON error
* Mobile app login succeeds in QC4

h2. Actual

* Transport failure — no HTTP response
* write ECONNRESET
* Mobile app login fails (see attachment)

h2. Impact

* Blocks Mobile1 auth smoke and member-session-dependent Mobile2 flows in QC4
* Blocks QC4 mobile regression / deployment gate validation

h2. Related tickets / comms

* RT: [https://rt.acs529.com/Ticket/Display.html?id=514351|https://rt.acs529.com/Ticket/Display.html?id=514351]
* DevOps Request channel — 2026-06-24
* KB: qa-automation-kb/mobile2-api-db-validation/ISSUES/06242026/

h2. Evidence

* MobileAuth Login failed - QC4.png
* Postman failing on auth endpoint.png

h2. Technical reference

* unite-mobile1: MobileMemberSessionStepdefs → POST mobilemembersession
* unite-accountowner: auth.service.ts → mobile1dataServiceUrl + mobilemembersession
* QC4 config: environment.qc4.ts → [unite-bff-wtn.qc4.unite529.com/mobile1api/v1/|http://unite-bff-wtn.qc4.unite529.com/mobile1api/v1/]
column251:

RT: https://rt.acs529.com/Ticket/Display.html?id=514351

Endpoint POST /mobile1api/v1/mobilemembersession — no longer ECONNRESET; returns expected session response.

Mobile login: OK in QC4 app.

RCA: QC4 requests to mobileapi.qc4.acs529.com for POST /mobile1api/v1/mobilemembersession were failing at the TCP/TLS layer with ECONNRESET because [unite-mobile1 BFF had no healthy backend behind the QC4 load balancer / ingress — e.g. pod crash loop, deployment rollback gap, or backend pool drained after a release]. h3. Why this spike existed

Before we could size or write migration stories for Unite Enrollment, we needed a fact-based picture of *where* automation lives today, *whether* it is trustworthy, and *what* blocks execution (IDP, env, local DB seeds). The program (QA-796 / UNITE MSC Test Automation) cannot migrate scenarios we have not inventoried. This spike was time-boxed discovery only — no migration implementation.

h3. Context sources reviewed (step by step)

# *Tech Demo* (Nizar, Nick, Luis — transcript in Tech Demo Meeting.txt): architecture, BFF vs core services, current Cucumber/integration test approach, IDP/OTP guidance, manual testing approach.
# *Prior team discussions* (MobileAutomation/General Docs): integration-test design (legacy suites not E2E; local Postgres *Datastore.sql*); Nick/Brian sprint estimates for Enrollment after Mobile1/Mobile2 setup.
# *Postman collections* (not legacy automation, but primary manual API reference — no org-standard collection per demo):
#* Luis: {{MSC Mobile app.postman_collection 3.json}}
#* Nick/Luis: {{Mobile App_boomerang.json}} (Boomerang export)
# *Program documentation* (qa-automation-kb): mobile-automation-program-hub, migration tracker template, RAID (DEC-1 pilot order, DEC-2 Cucumber vs Path B).

h3. Step-by-step activities performed

# Attended / reviewed UNITE MSC technical demo and captured enrollment as a *BFF microservice* (unite-enrollment) separate from mobile1/mobile2 and core services (auth, account, metadata, etc.).
# Confirmed *source system of record* for legacy tests: UniteMSC application repo (GitLab: ascensus-gs/products/unitemsc) — *read-only* for migration; exact enrollment service sub-path still to be confirmed on repo access.
# Documented *legacy automation pattern* from demo + integration-test design:
#* Per-service integration tests in app repos: {{mvn install -P debug}}, Cucumber + Cucable + Failsafe
#* Local Postgres seeded from committed {{*Datastore.sql}} snapshots
#* *Not running end-to-end today* — IdP and Universal Platform integrations never completed → suite is not a reliable regression signal
#* Even when historically green, tests were *environment-blind* (seed always matched code; shared QC4/Stage DB drift not detected)
# Recorded *manual testing reality* (Luis): no consolidated Postman collection; dev/QA maintain individual collections; focus on APIs under active development.
# Listed *enrollment-relevant manual API entry* from Luis collection: {{Enrollment - Validate}} → POST {{enrollmentapi/v1/enrollments/enrollment/bank-entered}} (encrypted event payload, Bearer JWT).
# Identified *gaps requiring follow-up* (not blockers to close spike): full file-level inventory (feature file count, step classes, SQL paths) pending read access + Infinity/QA-796 data per Brian’s note.

h3. Discovery findings — asset categories

||Category||Finding||Migration impact||
|Feature files / Cucumber scenarios|Exist in app repos near {{src/test}}; stale/unreliable per demo; E2E broken for IDP|Treat as *reference only* until re-validated in target framework|
|Step definitions|Rest Assured–style steps expected; possible app-repo coupling TBD on access|Map in QA-886; flag anti-patterns|
|Config / properties|QC4, Stage1, legacy IDP/UP assumptions likely|Must align to jsonapi-lib unite config pattern|
|SQL / DB validation|Tied to local seed DB in legacy model|Rewrite for shared QC4/Stage JDBC assertions|
|Test data|Heavy/encrypted payloads in requests (see Postman); not env-neutral|Externalize to test-data/ in migration stories|
|Runners / Maven profiles|{{debug}} profile pattern documented|Map to @smoke / @regression tags in target|
|Postman (Luis/Nick)|Supplementary; not automated legacy|Use for endpoint/payload baseline (QA-887)|

h3. Execution / trust status (legacy automation)

* *Last known reliable E2E:* No — IDP/UP incomplete (per integration-test design + demo).
* *Recommended use of legacy assets:* Reference for scenario ideas and coverage gaps — *not* production-ready regression.
* *OTP / 2FA:* Out of scope for MSC integration tests — disable 2FA on test accounts (Nizar/Luis); no API to fetch OTP.

h3. Top risks / blockers for downstream stories

# Repo read access to unitemsc enrollment paths — owner TBD
# DEC-1: Enrollment pilot vs Mobile2-first sequencing (Nick estimate vs program brief)
# DEC-2: Cucumber migration to API Automation Framework vs Path B (unite-msc TestNG zip)
# IDP migration in progress — legacy auth flows may still need coverage until Rajib confirms scope (Brian action item)
# Encryption on enrollment payloads — dependency on Mobile1 patterns per Nick estimate
# Consolidated Postman collection still open (Nizar/team follow-up from demo)

h3. Spike outputs (deliverables)

* Enrollment discovery notes captured in program hub: docs/mobile-automation-program-hub/05-unite-enrollment-migration-tracker.md (inventory table — counts TBD until repo access)
* RAID items updated conceptually: R1 stale tests, R2 IDP/config, R4 pilot order, R5 dual architecture
* Inputs ready for QA-886 (feature/step mapping framework) and QA-887 (endpoint catalog from Postman)

h3. Recommendation for next sprint stories (not in this spike)

# Story: Complete file-level inventory when repo access granted (feature count, step classes, SQL list)
# Story: Apply migration decision matrix per scenario (migrate/update/exclude/park)
# Story: Vertical slice 3–5 enrollment scenarios in API Automation Framework
# Spike/Task: Confirm with Rajib legacy vs IDP-only test scope during migration

h3. Spike acceptance — met?

Business/architecture context for enrollment automation documented Legacy test limitations documented with evidence (demo + design doc) Manual API reference sources identified (Luis/Nick Postman) Blockers and follow-ups listed for story creation File-level counts — deferred to next story pending repo access (explicit TBD)

✅

*Status:* Done — spike objective met; file-level inventory is a separate story dependency.

h2. Purpose

Support Naomi Bechar (Comet / CST) on validation of *QIPS-413 / AKD — TVG Calculator Credits* fix delivered under CST-469 (parent CST-472). Focus: *manual* verification that credit/guarantee ordering is deterministic after moving from SYSDATE to timestamps with *fractional seconds* (microsecond precision in Oracle terms).

h2. Context

* Comet Story CST-469: replace SYSDATE with LOCALTIMESTAMP in relevant XML; update existing data to include fractional seconds.
* Risk addressed: identical wall-clock second → non-deterministic ordering → wrong guarantee calculations.

h2. Scope (this QA Story)

* Author and execute *manual* test cases: UI/calculator (where Client Services checks apply) + *database* checks that CREATE_DT / UPDATE_DT (or equivalent column names) reflect *microsecond* changes on successive updates.
* Prepare *test data* and queries to prove: (1) initial insert has fractional part; (2) each update advances UPDATE timestamp with a *different* fractional second when updates occur in quick succession; (3) ordering of dependent calculations matches expected sequence.

h2. Out of scope

* Production deployment (Comet).
* Automated UI suite for TVG (optional follow-up Story unless requested).

h2. Dependencies

* Target environment + schema build containing CST-469 code and DB changes (confirm with Naomi: branch, env, ctl_ins_* objects).

column1: [V3][Daily-Regression][Flaky] Harden nightly suite — reduce intermittent failures
column35:
We need a focused effort to *stabilize the Unite/Prime nightly regression suite* so results are *consistent, trustworthy, and reproducible* in CI (remote nightly), not only on local machines.

Recent failures cluster into three themes:

# *Plan / auth model drift (IDP vs Non-IDP)*
Several plans (e.g. *MID*, *KSD*, and others) were moved or configured differently between *Non-IDP* and *IDP* behavior. Automation still assumes the old model (URLs, tags, suite XML grouping, or properties), which causes *wrong entry points or login flows* and *false failures* in regression.
# *Local pass vs nightly (remote) fail*
Some scenarios *pass locally* but *fail on the remote nightly job*. This indicates *environment, data, timing, parallelism, or configuration drift* rather than pure product defects. We have done *R&D* to narrow causes; we need *tracked fixes* so the same scenarios *pass in remote nightly* with clear evidence (logs, reports).
# *Flaky failures (timing / synchronization)*
A subset of failures is *intermittent*, often tied to *missing or insufficient waits*, dynamic UI, or async backend updates. We need *deterministic synchronization* (appropriate waits, stable locators, post-condition checks) without masking real defects.

column251:
*What broke*: Stage 1 again showed TLS/SSL failures (same class as QA-708): IDP (NYD/NMD), UE sub bene (login-dependent), CSR/member flows, legacy login/reg, transfers — symptoms looked like app breaks; SSLException: Received fatal alert: protocol_version in traces.

*Why*: Engineering traced the crash to the default RestClientFactory → SocketFactory path. SSLContext.getInstance("TLS") with no enabled-protocol pinning leaves negotiation to the JVM; protocol_version from the peer indicates the client offered a TLS version the server rejects (e.g. JVM/path still offering TLS 1.0/1.1 while the peer requires TLS 1.2+). Many monolith call sites use this path (~20+ managers/actions); standalone HTTP clients need separate fixes.

*What fixed Stage 1*: The TLS-related change was reverted (confirmed: change had been pushed again, then reverted); Stage 1 returned to normal operation.

Follow-up (engineering): Harden SocketFactory.getSSLContext (e.g. setEnabledProtocols TLSv1.2/TLSv1.3 or SSLContext.getInstance("TLSv1.2")) so all RestClientFactory.getRestClient(...) consumers inherit the fix; plan TLS 1.3 in prod with monolith changes, not flip alone on Java 8 clients.

Verification: QA confirmed legacy web reg (OKD, CAD), legacy web login (OKD, CAD), IDP login (NYD, NMD) — working post-revert.

column1: IDP - Enhance Prime v3 Framework for Deep Shadow DOM Element Handling in IDP Angular UI
column35:
The *IDP login and account recovery* flows in the Angular-based UI use *Shadow DOM encapsulation*, sometimes with multiple nested layers.
The current *Prime v3 Selenium 4 framework* supports the first-level Shadow DOM, but fails to detect elements nested deeper (e.g., *child-of-child* Shadow roots).

This spike aims to *research and evaluate solutions* for improving deep Shadow DOM element accessibility and identification — enabling automation to handle multi-level Shadow roots without manual workarounds or disabled MFA.

----

h3. *Objectives:*

# Review *current framework implementation* for Shadow DOM support.
# Identify *limitations* in Selenium 4’s Shadow root handling for nested elements.
# Explore third-party libraries or native WebDriver solutions to support:
#* *Recursive Shadow DOM traversal*
#* *Dynamic child/successor element discovery*
# Collaborate with *Sree Pallavi*, & *Nick (Framework Architect)* to assess adding this to the Prime core library.
# Create a *sample POC* demonstrating multi-layer Shadow DOM element detection.

----

h3. *Scope:*

* Applicable to *Prime v3 (Selenium 4)* and *IDP feature set*.
* Includes *login, password recovery, MFA, and error message* verification screens.
* Will evaluate:
** Selenium 4+ shadowRoot
** JavaScript executor approaches
** Custom utility wrappers

column35:
The Mobile 2 Contribution *GET by id* and *PUT* automation tests currently use hardcoded QC4 fixture values for path parameters:

* {{ext}} = {{"01"}}
* {{contributionId}} = {{"472560"}}

These values are defined in:

* {{mobile/mobile2/src/test/java/mobile2/contribution/MobileContributionDetailRequestTest.java}}
* {{mobile/mobile2/src/test/java/mobile2/contribution/MobileContributionPutRequestTest.java}}

*Affected endpoints:*

||Method||URL||
|GET|{{{{baseUrl}}/mobile2api/v1/mobilecontribution/{{ext}}/{{contributionId}}}}|
|PUT|{{{{baseUrl}}/mobile2api/v1/mobilecontribution/{{ext}}/{{contributionId}}}}|

Because {{ext}} and {{contributionId}} are environment-specific, the tests pass in QC4 but *fail in stage* (and other environments) when those IDs do not exist for the test user.

*Goal:* Update both tests to resolve {{ext}} and {{contributionId}} at runtime so they work across QC4, stage, and other configured environments—following the same automation-owned, dynamic pattern already used in {{MobileContributionPostRequestTest}} and {{MobileContributionDeleteRequestTest}}.

h3. Problem statement

Hardcoded path parameters tie tests to a single environment’s data. Stage uses different account extensions and contribution IDs, so GET/PUT calls return errors (e.g. 404/401) instead of exercising the API contract.

h3. Proposed approach

# Resolve {{ext}} dynamically from {{GET /mobile2api/v1/mobilecontribution}} → {{_embedded.item.mobileAccounts[0].ext}} (same as POST/DELETE).
# Obtain a valid {{contributionId}} dynamically by creating an automation-owned recurring contribution via POST (preferred, consistent with DELETE test), then use that id for GET detail and PUT update.
# Remove hardcoded {{ACCOUNT_EXT}} and {{CONTRIBUTION_ID}} constants.
# Optionally clean up created data after PUT (or document why cleanup is deferred).
column76:
* {{MobileContributionDetailRequestTest}} no longer uses hardcoded {{ext}} or {{contributionId}}.
* {{MobileContributionPutRequestTest}} no longer uses hardcoded {{ext}} or {{contributionId}}.
* Both tests resolve {{ext}} from {{GET mobilecontribution}} response.
* Both tests obtain {{contributionId}} dynamically (via POST create or other documented API flow).
* Tests pass in *QC4* ({{okdirect}}, user {{1}}).
* Tests pass in *stage* for the configured test user/branding.
* Assertions remain contract-focused (status, HAL {{_embedded.item}}, key business fields)—not tied to fixed QC4 IDs.
* No secrets, tokens, or PII added to code or tickets.
* Contribution integration suite ({{contribution-integration-testng.xml}}) includes both tests and runs green after change.

h3. Out of scope

* Changes to DELETE or POST tests (already dynamic).
* New negative/auth scenarios.
* SQL or DB-backed fixture lookups.

h3. Reference implementation

Use as pattern:

* {{MobileContributionPostRequestTest}} — dynamic {{seqAcctId}}, {{bnkId}}, {{beginDate}}

column251:
Symptom: Universal Enrollment and partial enrollment failed on Stage1 (V2 multi-module regression + V3 UE suite). UI showed connectivity issues / functionality not available; API returned HTTP 500 System error; automation reported Database results are empty.

Root cause: Inserts into UII0.TU_PERSON and UII0.TU_BENE failed because CTL_INS_DTTM was NULL. These columns are populated by database triggers (TRG_TU_PERSON_BIUR, TRG_TU_BENE_BIUR). Both triggers were disabled in the UII0 schema, so insert-time audit timestamps were not set → ORA-01400: cannot insert NULL into ("UII0"."TU_PERSON"."CTL_INS_DTTM") / ("UII0"."TU_BENE"."CTL_INS_DTTM") (ORA-06512).

Fix: Triggers re-enabled on affected tables in UII0 (Swapnil Patil). Enrollment/account-open path expected to succeed once triggers are active.

column1: [V2][Daily-Regression][Flaky] Harden nightly suite — reduce intermittent failures(post-spike)
column35:
We need a focused effort to *stabilize the Unite/Prime nightly regression suite* so results are *consistent, trustworthy, and reproducible* in CI (remote nightly), not only on local machines.

Recent failures cluster into three themes:

# *Plan / auth model drift (IDP vs Non-IDP)*
Several plans (e.g. *MID*, *KSD*, and others) were moved or configured differently between *Non-IDP* and *IDP* behavior. Automation still assumes the old model (URLs, tags, suite XML grouping, or properties), which causes *wrong entry points or login flows* and *false failures* in regression.
# *Local pass vs nightly (remote) fail*
Some scenarios *pass locally* but *fail on the remote nightly job*. This indicates *environment, data, timing, parallelism, or configuration drift* rather than pure product defects. We have done *R&D* to narrow causes; we need *tracked fixes* so the same scenarios *pass in remote nightly* with clear evidence (logs, reports).
# *Flaky failures (timing / synchronization)*
A subset of failures is *intermittent*, often tied to *missing or insufficient waits*, dynamic UI, or async backend updates. We need *deterministic synchronization* (appropriate waits, stable locators, post-condition checks) without masking real defects.
